request: why is the determinant of a rotation matrix always 1

beats.intent: The unit square on the grid with i-hat and j-hat
beats.narration: Start with the unit square, sitting on i-hat and j-hat. Its area is one.
beats.code:
stage.title("Rotations keep area")
p = draw_plane(stage)
i_hat, j_hat = draw_basis(stage, p)
sq = draw_unit_square(stage, p)
stage.caption("The unit square: area 1")

beats.intent: The whole grid turning a quarter turn, the square riding along
beats.narration: Rotate the plane by ninety degrees. The square moves, but it is the same square.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[0, -1], [1, 0]], riders=[sq, i_hat, j_hat])
stage.caption("A quarter turn: moved, not stretched")

beats.intent: A fresh grid turned by 30 degrees, the square's area read out as 1
beats.narration: Try a thirty degree turn. The square tilts, and its area is still exactly one.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
p2 = draw_plane(stage)
c, s = np.cos(PI / 6), np.sin(PI / 6)
sq2, area = show_determinant(stage, p2, [[c, -s], [s, c]])
stage.caption("Any angle: the area stays 1")

beats.intent: The rotation matrix's determinant worked out beside the grid
beats.narration: The determinant of a rotation is cos squared plus sin squared, which is always one.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\det\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta & -\sin\theta\\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta\end{bmatrix} = \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta", r"\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1", where="right")

request: what does a negative determinant mean? something about flipping the plane over?

beats.intent: i-hat, j-hat and the unit square on the grid
beats.narration: Going from i-hat to j-hat, you turn counterclockwise. Keep an eye on that.
beats.code:
stage.title("Negative determinants")
p = draw_plane(stage)
i_hat, j_hat = draw_basis(stage, p)
sq = draw_unit_square(stage, p)
stage.caption("i-hat to j-hat: counterclockwise")

beats.intent: The grid mirrored left to right, i-hat now pointing left
beats.narration: Now mirror the plane. i-hat points left, and going from i-hat to j-hat is now a clockwise turn.
beats.code:
apply_matrix(stage, p, [[-1, 0], [0, 1]], riders=[sq, i_hat, j_hat])
stage.caption("Mirrored: i-hat to j-hat is now clockwise")

beats.intent: A fresh grid where the unit square becomes a parallelogram of signed area -3
beats.narration: This matrix makes the square three times bigger and flips it over, so its determinant is minus three.
beats.code:
p2 = draw_plane(stage)
sq2, area = show_determinant(stage, p2, [[1, 2], [1, -1]])
stage.caption("Area 3, and flipped over")

beats.intent: The determinant computed: its size is the area, its sign the flip
beats.narration: One times minus one, minus two times one, is minus three: size three for the area, the minus sign for the flip.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\det\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix} = (1)(-1) - (2)(1)", r"\det\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix} = -3", where="right")
stage.caption("|det| is the area, the sign is the flip")
